dishes.name: Quiche Lorraine
dishes.desc: Shortcrust tart filled with eggs, crème fraîche and smoked bacon, with no cheese in the traditional version. The Moselle's classic dish, dating back to the 16th century.

dishes.name: Mirabelle tart
dishes.desc: Small golden mirabelle plums baked whole on a short pastry base. Lorraine grows most of the world's mirabelles, and the tart is eaten mainly in late summer.

dishes.name: Macarons de Boulay
dishes.desc: Chewy almond macarons of egg white, almond powder and sugar, made to the same recipe in the Moselle town of Boulay since 1854. About 30 minutes from Metz.

dishes.name: Madeleine de Commercy
dishes.desc: Small shell-shaped butter sponge cake from Commercy in the Meuse, said to have been improvised by a servant for Duke Stanislas. Sold as a Lorraine take-home treat.

dishes.name: Potée lorraine
dishes.desc: Winter pot of cabbage, carrots, potatoes, smoked sausages and pork shank simmered together. A hearty Lorraine farmhouse dish found on traditional menus.
